extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, research administrators, and scientists interested in peer review
extracted.subtask_short: NIH R01 review criteria and scoring
extracted.subtask_description: Description and analysis of the NIH R01 peer-review scored criteria and how assigned reviewers use them (five criterion scores plus an overall impact score, with integer 1–9 ratings). Includes guidance on application formatting and reviewer instructions introduced in the 2009/2010 changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the five core review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers provide an overall impact integer score (1–9) based largely on the five scored criteria and any additional applicable review criteria; reviewers synthesize criteria scores using their own discretion (no explicit rule translating criterion scores to overall impact). The average of the three assigned reviewers' overall impact scores determines whether applications are discussed; for discussed applications all committee members record an overall impact score, and composite averages/percentiles are produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims of the project are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will successful completion of the aims change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate how the project would advance the field; weak or poorly articulated significance can negatively affect other criterion scores (notably approach). In the analyzed data, significance scores were skewed (few '1' scores) and correlated with overall impact; if any criterion score is worse than '3 = Excellent,' the overall impact is very likely >3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the principal investigators, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If early stage investigators or new investigators are in the early stages of independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes PI and team expertise, prior accomplishments, training, and appropriateness for the proposed work; many investigator scores cluster at very good/excellent levels (30–40% scored as '1'). Investigator weaknesses can contribute to poorer approach scores (e.g., lack of biostatistical expertise or experience with patient populations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions? Are the concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions novel to one field of research or novel in a broad sense? Is a refinement, improvement, or new application of theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions proposed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates novelty and paradigm-shifting potential. Since 2009 applicants may explicitly state how their work is innovative; reviewers assigned good scores for innovation in a substantial fraction of critiques (e.g., ~11% scored '1'). The study found innovation scores are positively correlated with overall impact and found no evidence of an inverse relationship between innovation and overall impact. Innovation weaknesses can also depress approach scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If the project is in the early stages of development, will the strategy establish feasibility and will particularly risky aspects be managed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers experimental design, methods, procedures, and analytical plan; reviewers should focus on overall, general issues rather than routine methodological detail. Approach scores were the most broadly distributed and showed the strongest bivariate correlation with overall impact (but this may reflect greater variance/restricted range in other criteria). Weaknesses in other criteria (investigators, environment, significance, innovation) often manifest as weaknesses in the approach. Many common methodological problems (inadequate sample size/statistical power, poor reagent identification, confirmatory rather than rigorous tests) drive lower approach scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are the institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources available to the investigators adequate for the project proposed? Will the project benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers institutional support, facilities, resources, and special populations or collaborations. Environment scores frequently clustered at top values; lack of adequate resources or unique environment can reduce overall impact and interact with approach and investigator assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring System (1–9 descriptors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer scoring scale where lower numbers are better: 1 = Exceptional, 2 = Outstanding, 3 = Excellent, 4 = Very Good, 5 = Good, 6 = Satisfactory, 7 = Fair, 8 = Marginal, 9 = Poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assign integer scores (1–9) for each of the five core criteria and an overall impact score (thus six scores per assigned reviewer). Scores are averaged across assigned reviewers for preliminary rankings; for discussed applications all members' overall impact scores are averaged to a composite. The integer nature and range restriction (skewness, ceiling effects) complicate statistical analysis (non-normal distributions, heteroscedasticity, multicollinearity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria (human subjects, animals, biohazards, protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other review criteria (not separately scored) that reviewers are asked to consider include protections for human participants, adequacy of animal care and use, and appropriate handling and disposal of biohazardous materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are considered in determining the overall impact score but do not receive separate numeric criterion scores; when relevant, deficiencies in these areas should reduce the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Instructions, Logistics, and Use of Criterion Scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are recruited for expertise (usually serve voluntarily), applications are assigned to three in-depth reviewers who record five criterion scores and an overall impact score; reviewers are typically given ~6 weeks to review. Chartered study sections of 20–40 reviewers balance representation and determine which applications are discussed based on average preliminary overall impact scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers were instructed (post-2010 changes) to focus on overall, general issues and not routine methodological detail; reviewers use their own judgment to synthesize the five criterion scores into an overall impact score. Procedural norms (three assigned reviewers, averaging, discussion cutoffs, percentiling) impact how scores translate into funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Formatting and Presentation (guidance to applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application format changes (since 2010) reduced the Research Strategy from 25 to 12 pages and instructed applicants to explicitly describe how their application meets each review criterion, including innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to explicitly address the five criteria within the shorter Research Strategy; clearer communication and explicit formatting addressing each criterion may improve reviewer ability to evaluate criteria and could reduce ambiguous/unintended ceiling or floor effects. The format change aims to shift reviewer focus away from excessive methodological detail toward broader impact and innovation.
